reasoning_summary: Checked every step in order for n=1012, ground set [2024]. Construction (0005-0009): |A|=|B|=506, |C|=|D|=506 partitioning [2024]; A∪C, A∪D, B∪C, B∪D each have 1012 elements, are distinct, and every triple of them meets in the empty set (e.g. (A∪C)∩(A∪D)=A and A∩(B∪C)=∅), so 4 is attainable. Upper bound (0015-0033): incidence matrix has 2n=2024 columns, ∑c_i=kn=1012k, so the column average is k/2; ∑C(c_i,3) ≥ 2n·C(k/2,3) is legitimate via the convexified g(x)=0 for x≤2, x(x-1)(x-2)/6 for x>2 (g is convex, agrees with C(c,3) at nonnegative integers) as noted in 0070. The 3-wise intersection condition gives ≤1 column-triple per row-triple, hence ≤C(k,3) total. Combining and cancelling k(k-2)/6>0 gives n(k-4)≤4(k-1), i.e. 2n ≤ 8(k-1)/(k-4) for k≥5, matching 0029. Since (k-1)/(k-4) is strictly decreasing for k>4, its maximum over k≥5 is at k=5, giving RHS=32 < 2024, so no k≥5 is possible and k≤4; independent sanity check: k=5 forces ∑c_i=5060 over 2024 columns, whose minimum ∑C(c_i,3) (1012 columns with c=3, 1012 with c=2) is 1012, far exceeding C(5,3)=10. So the answer 4 is correct and the argument establishing it is sound. Two defects are present but neither breaks the proof of the asked claim: (i) line 0031 is garbled — the RHS at k=5 is 8·4/1=32, not 8·5/1=40, and the asserted direction '40 > 2·1012' is false; the needed and true fact is 32 < 2024, which is exactly what yields the contradiction the author draws in 0033; (ii) line 0055, inside the non-load-bearing BONUS aside about n=3, misstates the equality condition: with k=10 subsets of size 3 there are 30 incidences over 6 elements, so each element lies in exactly 5 subsets, and the author's own list in 0059 puts element 1 in {1,2,3},{1,3,4},{1,4,5},{1,5,6},{1,6,2} — 5 subsets, not 3. Line 0057 (every pair in exactly 2 subsets) is correct and is the actual equality condition of the pair count in 0041-0045, which I verified (k·C(n,2) ≤ 2·C(2n,2) gives k ≤ 4(2n-1)/(n-1) = 10 at n=3), as is the 10-set construction (all 15 pairs occur exactly twice, so no 3 sets share 2 elements) and the OP argument in 0065-0066. Since the theorem posed (maximum = 4 for 1012-subsets of [2024]) is correctly proved end to end, verdict VALID; the two slips above are a transparent numeric typo and an incorrect remark in an appendix.
